title: Chunks before the final round
statement: Let $R$ be a natural number and let $G$ assign a CNF formula over natural-number variables to each natural-number index. For every natural number $j\le R$, concatenating the chunks at indices $0,\ldots,j-1$ gives exactly the fragment formed from the concatenation of the formulas $G(0),\ldots,G(j-1)$.
hypotheses_covered: A family $G$ of CNF formulas indexed by natural numbers
replaced: Let $R$ be the last round index and let a family assign a clause group to each round. For every $j \le R$, the concatenation of the chunks of rounds $0,\dots,j-1$ equals the serialized fragment of the concatenation of the first $j$ groups, so no formula terminator appears in a proper prefix of the rounds.
